title: Pink Paradise
content: Pink Paradise is a compact bush rose with delicate pink petals that brighten any small space. Growing to just 0.6–0.8 metres, it is perfect for containers on balconies, patios, and small courtyard gardens. Its sweet and light fragrance carries gently in the breeze, making it an ideal companion plant near seating areas. For best results, plant in well-drained soil with at least six hours of direct sunlight. Water regularly during summer and apply a slow-release rose fertiliser in early spring. Deadheading spent blooms encourages continuous flowering from spring through to autumn. This variety shows good disease resistance but benefits from occasional preventative fungicide application in humid climates.

title: Coral Dream
content: Coral Dream is an eye-catching coral-coloured rose with exceptional disease resistance, growing to a compact 0.5–0.7 metres. It thrives in containers and adds warmth to any garden setting with its unique coral hue. The mild citrus-scented fragrance adds a refreshing note to outdoor dining areas. This variety is a summer bloomer that produces clusters of semi-double flowers. Botanically, its disease resistance comes from careful hybridisation, making it virtually immune to common fungal diseases like black spot and powdery mildew. It prefers slightly acidic soil (pH 6.0–6.5) and benefits from mulching to retain moisture during hot summer months. Prune lightly in late winter to encourage bushy growth and abundant flowering.

title: Fairytale Magic
content: Fairytale Magic (Märchenzauber) is a Kordes-bred floribunda that won the prestigious Golden Rose of Baden-Baden award in 2016. Growing to approximately 60–100 cm, it produces nostalgic, double-petalled blooms in a soft pink shade that deepens towards the centre, with an enchanting strong fruity fragrance. The blooms are exceptionally large for a floribunda, often bigger than the stem itself. In autumn, it develops decorative rose hips (rosa canina) that add winter interest to the garden. Plant in a sheltered position with full sun and enrich the soil with well-rotted compost before planting. This rose performs superbly in containers near fences, earning it a spot as one of the finest modern floribundas. Its outstanding health rating makes it virtually maintenance-free.

title: Bengali
content: Bengali is an ADR-certified Kordes floribunda, awarded the Allgemeine Deutsche Rosenneuheitenprüfung rating in 2010 for the best disease resistance among all orange-hued roses. It produces large, cupped double blooms in an intense apricot-orange shade that softens to salmon-pink as the flowers mature. The fragrance is a sweet blend of apricot and apple-lemon notes, strongest in the early morning hours. Growing to approximately 1 metre tall and 50 cm wide, Bengali is a reliable repeat-flowering variety blooming from late spring to early autumn. Its compact, upright habit with glossy dark green foliage makes it suitable for beds, borders, and training along fences. Water deeply once a week, feed with potassium-rich fertiliser monthly, and deadhead regularly to encourage successive flushes throughout the season.

title: Coral Lions-Rose®
content: Coral Lions-Rose® is a Kordes Fantasia® floribunda introduced in 2019, awarded the prestigious ADR certificate in 2020 for exceptional disease resistance. The medium-sized (7–8 cm), cup-shaped double flowers open in a vibrant coral-salmon hue, gradually deepening to apricot-orange towards the centre. As blooms age, the outermost petals fade to a creamy ivory-pink, creating a beautiful multi-tonal effect. Buds are noticeably darker orange than the open flowers. Growing 0.8–1.2 metres tall and 50 cm wide, this variety has a bushy, upright habit perfect for borders, beds, and larger containers near fences. The light herbal fragrance is subtle but pleasant. Plant in full sun with good air circulation, and water at the base to avoid wetting the foliage. It has won numerous international prizes, including medals in Lyon, Le Roeulx, Kortrijk, and Warsaw.

title: White Elegance
content: White Elegance is a stunning pure white bush rose that creates an elegant border in any garden setting. Growing to 1.3–1.5 metres, it is a tall and stately variety that is both hardy and reliable, with beautiful high-centred form and excellent disease resistance. The delicate, sweet fragrance carries well in sheltered positions. Botanically, its repeat-flowering habit is remarkable, producing pristine white blooms virtually year-round in temperate climates. The long stems make White Elegance ideal as a cut flower — the blooms last up to ten days in a vase. Plant in rich, loamy soil amended with organic matter. Prune established plants by one-third in late winter, removing any dead or crossing canes. Due to its height, it works beautifully as a flowering hedge, providing both privacy and continuous floral beauty throughout the seasons.

title: Crimson Majesty
content: Crimson Majesty is a majestic bush rose featuring deep crimson blooms with velvety petals that catch the light beautifully. Growing 1.4–1.6 metres tall, it creates dramatic borders and commanding focal points in any garden. The rich, intense fragrance is among the strongest of all red roses, filling the garden with its classic damask scent. For a successful planting, dig a hole twice the width of the root ball and mix in well-rotted manure. Position the bud union just below soil level and water deeply after planting. This variety benefits from hard pruning in late winter — cut back to three or four outward-facing buds per cane to encourage vigorous spring growth. Apply a balanced rose fertiliser every four to six weeks during the growing season. Due to its height and density, Crimson Majesty is perfect for creating a tall, floriferous hedge that provides both colour and privacy.

title: Royal Climber
content: Royal Climber is a vigorous climbing rose with abundant blooms, reaching an impressive 2.5–3.5 metres. It is perfect for covering walls, fences, and arbors with a spectacular floral display of pink and red blooms. Its sweet and strong fragrance creates an intoxicating garden atmosphere. When planting a climbing rose, install your support structure first — a sturdy trellis, wire system, or pergola rated for the mature weight. Plant 30 cm from the base of the wall to ensure adequate root moisture. Train the main canes horizontally by tying them loosely with garden twine; this forces lateral shoots which produce the most flowers. During the first two years, do not prune the main canes — only remove spent flower clusters. From the third year onwards, prune laterals back to two or three buds in late winter. Feed monthly during the growing season and water deeply, especially during dry spells.

title: Sunset Vine
content: Sunset Vine is a stunning climbing rose with gradient blooms that transition from warm orange at the centre to soft yellow at the petal tips. Growing 3.0–4.0 metres, it creates a breathtaking sunset effect on vertical structures with continuous flowering from summer through autumn. The citrus and honey fragrance is especially prominent on warm evenings. Botanically, this bicolour effect is caused by differential anthocyanin and carotenoid distribution in the petal cells, which shifts as the bloom matures. Sunset Vine excels on south-facing or west-facing walls where it receives maximum afternoon warmth. It is more tolerant of partially shaded conditions than many climbing roses. The canes are moderately flexible, making them easier to train along arches and pergolas. Apply a potassium-rich fertiliser in mid-summer to intensify the sunset colour effect. Mulch heavily in winter to protect the root zone from frost damage.

title: Snow Cascade
content: Snow Cascade is a graceful white climbing rose with cascading blooms, reaching 2.8–3.8 metres. It is exceptional for creating a romantic white garden with year-round interest, as it blooms virtually every season in mild climates. The light, fresh fragrance adds to its ethereal charm without being overwhelming. What makes Snow Cascade unique among climbers is its nearly thornless canes, making it safe and pleasant to handle during pruning and training. To create a romantic white garden, plant Snow Cascade alongside white lavender and silver-foliaged plants like lamb's ear. Install a strong archway or obelisk before planting, and train the young canes in a fan shape for maximum coverage. Water consistently during the first year to establish a deep root system. Once established, this variety is remarkably drought-tolerant. Prune after the main flush of flowers by removing spent blooms and shortening side shoots to encourage the next wave of pristine white cascading blooms.

title: Essential Rose Planting Guide
content: Successfully growing roses begins with proper site selection and planting technique. Roses require at least 6–8 hours of direct sunlight daily. In extremely hot climates, some afternoon shade can prevent flower damage. They thrive in well-drained, fertile soil rich in organic matter (pH 6.0–7.0). Dig a hole twice as wide as the container and at least 18 inches deep. Mix the native soil with compost or well-rotted manure (50/50 mix). Position the rose so the bud union is at the appropriate depth: 1–2 inches below the surface in cold climates, or at soil level in mild climates. Water thoroughly immediately after planting and maintain consistent moisture for the first few weeks.

title: Advanced Botanical Tips
content: Understanding the botanical needs of your roses ensures long-term health. Roses prefer deep, infrequent watering over light daily sprinkles. Provide about 1 inch of water per week, always at the base; avoid wetting the foliage to prevent fungal diseases like black spot. Early morning is the best time for hydration. Apply a 2–3 inch layer of organic mulch to retain moisture and suppress weeds, keeping it away from the main stem. Annual pruning in early spring is vital—remove dead, diseased, or crossing canes and open the center of the plant to improve airflow. Make cuts at a 45-degree angle above an outward-facing bud.
